hunks.baseline: That came with a single remark from a high-ranking official who introduced himself as the person in charge of the investigation.
hunks.sol: The high-ranking official who introduced himself as the lead investigator had just one thing to say.

hunks.baseline: “Additional investigations related to this case will be conducted, so we ask for your continued cooperation in the future.”
hunks.sol: “We’ll be conducting further inquiries into this case. Please cooperate with us if we contact you again.”

hunks.baseline: According to Team Leader Choi’s investigation, Michael Silbert’s influence reached the leadership of countries all over the world. Switzerland, in particular, was a tax haven for his astronomical wealth.
hunks.sol: According to Team Leader Choi, Michael Silbert’s influence reached the leaders of countries across the world. Switzerland, in particular, was where he sheltered his astronomical wealth from taxes.

hunks.baseline: And Team Leader Choi neatly cleared up the question I had raised.
hunks.sol: Team Leader Choi had a straightforward answer.

hunks.baseline: “They deliberately let us go. Since it was clear that neither the evidence nor the circumstances had anything to do with us, they must have judged that pursuing the matter any further would be difficult.”
hunks.sol: “He deliberately let us go. There’s no evidence or circumstance connecting us to the death. He must have decided he couldn’t push this any further.”

hunks.baseline: “That bastard Michael let us go on purpose? Just getting dragged into this case would already hurt us.”
hunks.sol: “Michael decided that? Just getting dragged into the case would hurt us.”

hunks.baseline: “The public is fickle. Right now, quite a few people are cursing us because they’re being controlled by the media and mob psychology. But that’s because The Prophet and terrorism provide a plausible justification at first glance.”
hunks.sol: “The public is fickle. Right now, plenty of people are cursing us, swayed by the media and the crowd. But The Prophet and the terrorist attacks give them a reason that seems plausible at first glance.”

hunks.baseline: “And if the justification isn’t convincing, the public won’t let itself be fooled?”
hunks.sol: “And if the reason doesn’t hold up, people won’t buy it?”

hunks.baseline: “Human beings have acted according to justifications for thousands of years. But if such an important justification begins to waver, many of the people who were criticizing us will change sides.”
hunks.sol: “People have acted on what they consider justified for thousands of years. If that justification falls apart, a good number of those condemning us will change sides.”

hunks.baseline: Come to think of it, that was a pattern people displayed often—no, quite frequently.
hunks.sol: Come to think of it, people did that all the time.

hunks.baseline: You could see it everywhere just by looking at the entertainment news posted on online portals.
Whenever a celebrity became embroiled in controversy, countless netizens swarmed them like bees and clung to the honey dripped by the media.
hunks.sol: You only had to look at the entertainment news on any online portal. The moment a celebrity got caught up in a scandal, netizens swarmed like bees to the honey the media had put out.

hunks.baseline: There were the genius prophets who claimed they had known it would happen ever since the celebrity’s debut, and even twenty-first-century physiognomists insisting that face-reading was a science.
hunks.sol: There were the genius prophets who claimed they’d known what the celebrity was like from the day they debuted, and the twenty-first-century face-readers insisting that appearances were science.

hunks.baseline: And around the time the winner of that world’s greatest malicious-comment contest was crowned by upvotes, a new fact would emerge and turn the situation around, and the swarm would change its tune in an instant.
hunks.sol: By the time upvotes had crowned a winner in the world’s greatest nasty-comment contest, some new fact would come out and turn the story on its head. The whole swarm would change its tune.

hunks.baseline: Why did they do that?
hunks.sol: Why?

hunks.baseline: It was simple.
hunks.sol: Simple.

hunks.baseline: *Because they no longer had an excuse to keep cursing them.*
hunks.sol: *They had no excuse to keep cursing them.*

hunks.sol: Siegfried Wassmann’s mysterious death was that kind of case. Michael Silbert understood how people worked, and he knew exactly when to press on and when to stop.

hunks.baseline: “Michael is, in a word, a mad bastard.”
hunks.sol: “Michael is, in a word, a madman.”

hunks.baseline: Magic Johnson abruptly broke the silence in a subdued voice.
hunks.sol: Magic Johnson broke the silence, his voice subdued.

hunks.baseline: “But the biggest reason we need to be wary of him is that this mad bastard is more meticulous and stronger than anyone.”
hunks.sol: “But the greatest reason to be wary of him is that he’s also meticulous and powerful.”

hunks.baseline: “I agree. When I first saw that bastard in Paris, I felt something so eerie that it was difficult to believe he was human.”
hunks.sol: “I agree. When I first saw him in Paris, I felt something so chilling that I could scarcely believe he was human.”

hunks.baseline: Most madmen ended up in prison or a mental hospital.

hunks.sol: But when a madman like Michael had everything, the world had another name for him.

hunks.baseline: The powerful.

hunks.baseline: But that bastard…

hunks.sol: Michael had gone beyond them.

hunks.baseline: A madman you’d get only by adding those two together—and then multiplying them.
hunks.sol: You’d have to add those two together, then multiply the result, to get a madman like him.

hunks.baseline: Michael Silbert was a monster who had given up on remaining human.

hunks.baseline: *Why? What could he possibly want to go this far?*
hunks.sol: *Why? What could he possibly want badly enough to go this far?*

hunks.baseline: I raised my head with those questions in mind. The sky was clear as hell, and the surrounding scenery, which still retained the beauty of northern Europe, was beautiful in contrast to the situation we were in.
hunks.sol: I looked up. The sky was clear as hell, and the surrounding landscape had kept its northern European beauty. It couldn’t have been more at odds with what was happening.

hunks.baseline: I muttered a quiet curse inwardly, then pulled a small pouch from inside my clothes and handed it to Magic Johnson.
hunks.sol: I cursed under my breath, then pulled a small pouch from inside my clothes and handed it to Magic Johnson.

hunks.baseline: “Don’t open it now. Take it with you and examine it carefully. Team Leader Choi and I are both hopeless with magic, so we wouldn’t understand much even if we looked at it.”
